title: Team Scrimmage
story: Two teams play a real, coach-managed match, just like game day.
setup: Split the full practice space in half with a mini goal at each end. Use bibs to form two even teams and keep a spare ball at each sideline for fast restarts.
instructions: Play two teams using the same restarts as game day: no goal kicks, corner kicks or throw-ins; coaches or goalkeepers reintroduce the ball.
Rotate the goalkeeper role at least once during each half.
Play the first half; keep interruptions brief and restart quickly.
At halftime, take a short water break, switch ends and adjust teams only if needed for balance.
Play the second half; note effort, enjoyment and independent decisions rather than the score.
coach_lens: Watch for the behaviors from today's core activities appearing on their own in the run of play, without a coach prompt.
questions: What did we practice today that you used in the scrimmage?

simplify: Play with an extra attacker to create more scoring chances.
challenge: Add a second ball briefly to increase decisions.
Introduce one new restart rule from your league's handbook.
low_attendance: Play continuous 3v3 or 4v4 with no substitutions.
high_attendance: Run two scrimmage fields at once so no one waits on the sideline.
limited_equipment: Use cone gates in place of mini goals.

safety: Rotate goalkeepers so no player is in goal for the entire session.
Keep spare balls off the field of play, at the sideline only.

source.title: Play-Practice-Play
source.reviewer_notes: Coach-authored, field-tested closing scrimmage applying U.S. Soccer's Play-Practice-Play principle that game-realistic play is itself the primary teaching tool, run under the league's own match-day restart rules. No source wording or artwork reproduced.
